Carcinoma renale papillare: massa ipovas: Papillary renal carcinoma: hypovascular and homogeneous mass
Uomo di 73 anni. Massa renale sinistra r: 73-year-old man. Left renal mass found on ultrasound. Abdominal CT in three phases (unenhanced, corticomedullary, delayed).
Referta in ordine: massa, comportamento: Report in order: mass, contrast behavior, conclusion.
Un aumento di densità di almeno 20 HU do:
An increase in density of at least 20 HU after contrast indicates enhancing solid tissue; between 10 and 20 HU the finding is equivocal, and papillary tumors often fall right here: a papillary tumor can be mistaken for a hyperdense cyst if unenhanced and post-contrast images are not compared in the same region (ROI).
Differential diagnosis of solid renal masses without fat: clear cell carcinoma is hypervascular and heterogeneous (necrosis); papillary is hypovascular and homogeneous (weak and slow enhancement, often < 20-30 HU); chromophobe has intermediate, homogeneous enhancement, sometimes a central scar like oncocytoma, from which it cannot be distinguished on imaging; lipid-poor angiomyolipoma is often hyperdense on unenhanced images. Infiltrative lesions that preserve the shape of the kidney suggest urothelial carcinoma, lymphoma, metastasis or pyelonephritis, not a typical renal carcinoma.
To measure enhancement, the ROI is placed in the same area of the mass in all phases, avoiding edges and calcifications.
Massa renale omogenea che si impregna po: Homogeneous renal mass with weak and slow enhancement: think of papillary carcinoma (and do not call it a cyst without comparing the phases).
Carcinoma renale papillare, ISUP 2, pT3: Papillary renal carcinoma, ISUP 2, pT3 (clinical data from the C4KC-KiTS collection; pathologic size 5.4 cm).
